evals.prompt: Write a single self-contained index.html (no bundler) that loads a glTF model from ./assets/robot.glb with Draco compression, shows it on a ground plane with a shadow, lets me orbit with the mouse, and plays the model's first animation clip. Use the current three.js version from a CDN import map.
evals.expected_output: One HTML file using an import map pinned to three@0.186.x, three/addons imports (GLTFLoader, DRACOLoader with decoder path, OrbitControls with damping + update), renderer with shadows enabled, DirectionalLight with castShadow and a sized shadow camera, ground receiveShadow, AnimationMixer updated with a Timer/Clock delta in setAnimationLoop, resize handler, sRGB/tone mapping correct, no deprecated APIs (outputEncoding, sRGBEncoding, examples/js, Geometry).
assertions: Import map pins three@0.186.x and uses three/addons/ paths
Uses DRACOLoader with an explicit setDecoderPath
Shadows: shadowMap.enabled, light castShadow, ground receiveShadow, meshes castShadow
AnimationMixer plays gltf.animations[0] and is updated with a frame delta in the loop
OrbitControls with enableDamping and controls.update() per frame
Resize handler updates camera aspect, projection matrix and renderer size
No deprecated APIs (outputEncoding, sRGBEncoding, Clock without note, PCFSoftShadowMap, examples/js)
Environment lighting or correct tone mapping so glTF PBR is not dark

evals.prompt: My three.js scene: I load a texture with TextureLoader and put it on a MeshStandardMaterial but it looks washed out and way too bright compared to the PNG. Also when I later change `mesh.material.map = otherTexture` nothing updates. What's wrong and how do I fix it? I'm on the latest three.
evals.expected_output: Explains texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace for color maps (ColorManagement on by default, outputColorSpace default sRGB), mentions tone mapping/exposure as second suspect, and explains material.needsUpdate = true is required when adding a map after first compile (define change), not texture.needsUpdate. No mention of the removed `encoding` API as a fix.

evals.prompt: I have a three.js app where the user can click on any of ~50 boxes to select it (highlight it) and drag it around on the ground plane. Show me how to implement picking and dragging with the current three.js API, including touch.
evals.expected_output: Raycaster.setFromCamera with NDC from pointer events (pointerdown/move/up, works for touch), intersectObjects, highlighting via material/emissive change, dragging by intersecting a ground Plane (THREE.Plane or ray.intersectPlane) or using DragControls from three/addons, disabling OrbitControls while dragging; uses current API names only.
